title: Theatre Royal
paragraphs: British literary-adaptation anthology produced by Harry Alan Towers for international syndication. The frozen 45-recording set carries OTRR sequence labels 1-48 with three gaps; secondary references disagree on total produced count, so sequence labels remain archive provenance rather than canonical production numbering.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Laurence Olivier-hosted first series (October 4, 1953 to April 18, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Ralph Richardson-hosted second series (April 25, 1954 to September 1, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Harry Alan Towers (producer and director), Sidney Torch (music and music director), Derek Patmore (radio adaptor), Laurence Olivier (host, performer, and narrator), Ralph Richardson (host, performer, and narrator), Campbell Singer (performer), and Charles Dickens (author).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]].

The stories often return to classic literature and literary source, radio dramatization and adaptation, British stage and screen performance tradition, crime, guilt and moral transgression, supernatural, uncanny and gothic fiction, and social satire and class manners.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes British literary radio made for international transcription syndication, Prestige British stage and screen talent on radio, Classic literature adapted for postwar radio audiences, and Olivier-to-Richardson host succession.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]], [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]], and [[show|the-fred-allen-show|The Fred Allen Show]].
